title: How to use version converter on a large (>2GB) model?
body:
# Ask a Question

### Question
I have a model with external weights. The size of the external weights file is larger than 2GB.
If I run the converter with
```
original_model = onnx.load(model_path)
converted_model = version_converter.convert_version(original_model, 21)
```
then the converter runs into an error (even though the error itself is a bit misleading `RuntimeError: /github/workspace/onnx/common/ir_pb_converter.cc:716: assertNonNull: Assertion `g.get() != nullptr` failed: Warning: onnx version converter is unable to parse input model. (The IR version of the ONNX model may be too old.)`)


If I skip loading the external weights:
```
original_model = onnx.load(model_path, load_external_data=False)
converted_model = version_converter.convert_version(original_model, 21)
```
then the weights in the converted model do not have file location info anymore so the model becomes unusable.

Is there a way to work around this issue?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Here's an artificial example where the model is very simple but it contains a weight tensor that exceeds 2GB. Running the following script will export the model.

If you run `onnx.inliner.inline_local_functions()` on it you will see what I described above:
- If you load the model with `load_external_data=True` the output file has an empty graph.
- If you load it with `load_external_data=False` no inlining happens (Although for this artificial example the behavior is slightly different from the real model I described above where no inlining happens and the local function subgraph disappears)

```
import onnx_graphsurgeon as gs
import onnx
import numpy as np

dtype = np.float32
X = gs.Variable(name="X", dtype=dtype, shape=(1,1))

Y = gs.Constant(name="Y", values=np.zeros((20000,30000), dtype=dtype))
Add_out = gs.Variable(name="Add_out")
Z = gs.Variable(name="Z", dtype=np.int64)

node_identity = gs.Node(op="Add", inputs=[X, Y], outputs=[Add_out])
node_local = gs.Node(op="LocalFunction", inputs=[Add_out], outputs=[Z], attrs={"axis":1}, domain="trt")

graph = gs.Graph(nodes=[node_identity, node_local], inputs=[X, Y], outputs=[Z], opset=20)


# Register local function
def register_ops():
    @gs.Graph.register()
    def constant(self, *args, **kwargs):
        available_attrs = [
            "sparse_value",
            "value",
            "value_float",
            "value_floats",
            "value_int",
            "value_ints",
            "value_string",
            "value_strings",
        ]
        found_attrs = sum(
            1 for available_attr in available_attrs if available_attr in kwargs
        )
        assert (
            found_attrs == 1
        ), f"Exactly 1 attribute must be specified for op Constant. Got {found_attrs}"

        out = self.layer(op="Constant", outputs=["constant_out"], attrs=kwargs)[0]
        return out

    @gs.Graph.register()
    def shape(self, x):
        out = self.layer(
            op="Shape",
            inputs=[x],
            outputs=["shape_out"],
        )[0]
        return out

    @gs.Graph.register()
    def gather(self, x, indices, axis=0):
        out = self.layer(
            op="Gather",
            inputs=[x, indices],
            outputs=["gather_out"],
            attrs={"axis": axis},
        )[0]
        return out

def register_local_function(graph):
    local_input = gs.Variable("local_input", shape=[-1, -1])

    local_func = gs.Function(
        "LocalFunction",
        domain="trt",
        inputs=[local_input],
        opset=21,
        attrs={"axis": None},
    )

    axis_constant_out_1 = local_func.constant(
        value_int=gs.Node.AttributeRef("axis", int)
    )
    input_shape = local_func.shape(local_input)

    shape_at_axis = local_func.gather(input_shape, axis_constant_out_1, axis=0)
    local_func.outputs.append(shape_at_axis)

    graph.functions.append(local_func)

register_ops()
register_local_function(graph)

model = gs.export_onnx(graph)
onnx.save(model, "test_clean.onnx", save_as_external_data=True)
```

comments.body: I see this is a large constant node. You would need to convert the tensor to external data before calling infer shapes. Anytime you give infer_shapes a proto with more than 2gb of data it will fail. The idea is always finding ways to change the proto to be less than 2gb. In this case you can call the external data helper to convert to external tensor

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I investigated the problem @reporter is having a bit further.

I was able to reproduce the problem using only native ONNX code:

```python
import onnx
import numpy as np
from onnx import TensorProto

# Random data
np.random.seed(42)
random_shape = (20000,30000)  # Approx 2.4 GB
random_data = np.random.rand(*random_shape).astype(np.float32)
print(f"Data size in GB: {random_data.nbytes / (1024**3):.2f} GB")

# Create two initializer nodes: one for the data tensor, second is just a scalar 1
initializer_tensor = onnx.helper.make_tensor(
    name="initializer_tensor",
    data_type=onnx.TensorProto.FLOAT,
    dims=list(random_shape),
    vals=random_data.flatten(),
)
initializer_scalar = onnx.helper.make_tensor(
    name="initializer_scalar",
    data_type=onnx.TensorProto.FLOAT,
    dims=[],
    vals=[1.0],
)

# Define a graph with simple addition
add_node = onnx.helper.make_node(
    "Add",
    inputs=["initializer_tensor", "initializer_scalar"],
    outputs=["sum_output"]
)

# WILL CRASH ON THIS LINE WITH google.protobuf.message.DecodeError: Error parsing message with type 'onnx.TensorProto'
graph_def = onnx.helper.make_graph(
    name="SimpleAddition",
    nodes=[add_node],
    inputs=[],
    outputs=[
        onnx.helper.make_tensor_value_info("sum_output", TensorProto.FLOAT, list(random_shape))
    ],
    initializer=[initializer_tensor, initializer_scalar]
)

# Save model to file
model_filename = "test_simple_add.onnx"
opset_imports=[onnx.helper.make_opsetid("", 21)]
model_def = onnx.helper.make_model(graph_def, opset_imports=opset_imports)
model_def.ir_version = 10
onnx.save(model_def, model_filename)
print(f"ONNX model saved as {model_filename}")

onnx.checker.check_model(model_filename)
print("ONNX model is valid")
```

It seems to me that the problem stems from the fact that it isn't his whole model which is >2GB, but a single initializer value.

The problem can be traced further into how ONNX uses protobuf objects to store initializer data:

```python
import numpy as np
from onnx import TensorProto, GraphProto

# Random data
np.random.seed(42)
random_shape = (20000,30000)  # Approx 2.4 GB
random_data = np.random.rand(*random_shape).astype(np.float32)
print(f"Data size in GB: {random_data.nbytes / (1024**3):.2f} GB")

tensor = TensorProto()
tensor.data_type = 1
tensor.name = "initializer_tensor"
tensor.float_data.extend(random_data.flat)
tensor.dims.extend(random_shape)

graph = GraphProto()
graph.initializer.extend([tensor])
```

This is essentially what ONNX is trying to do and the last line causes the protobuf `DecodeError`.

This is a limitation of Protobuf for which we currently do not have a workaround.

comments.body:
We have quite a few onnx models bigger than 2gb running in one of our test suites: <https://github.com/nod-ai/SHARK-TestSuite/tree/main/alt_e2eshark>. Version updating is very useful for us, since we need the updated shape inference functions available at newer opset versions. Since updating the opset version for these models fails when loading the external data, I've occasionally hacked around this by:

1. loading model without external data
2. Performing version update (destroys external data references)
3. tracing through the old model and collecting all external data references (initializers and node attributes)
4. copying them over to the new model

You can see this implemented in <https://github.com/nod-ai/SHARK-TestSuite/blob/949ef993885e3941e20a496f0c0330d24b74489c/alt_e2eshark/onnx_tests/models/nlp.py#L84-L114>. 

In general, I was wondering why it is necessary to load external data for the version-updating tool. Are there certain ops which need knowledge of external data to update properly?

comments.body:
Okay, I'm guessing a bit here, but 

<https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/a952ab0e15884f4aa1d67ef935c3e691ae78c061/onnx/version_converter/convert.cc#L124>

calls

<https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/3d5acaf3e23ae8db7ac01b8cfedb17b8817121f4/onnx/common/ir_pb_converter.cc#L391>

calls

<https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/3d5acaf3e23ae8db7ac01b8cfedb17b8817121f4/onnx/common/ir_pb_converter.cc#L229>

which does:

<https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/3d5acaf3e23ae8db7ac01b8cfedb17b8817121f4/onnx/common/ir_pb_converter.cc#L288-L289>

And as far as I can grok from this, `tensorProtoToTensor` doesn't handle external data. 

My understanding after skimming some of the codebase is that `TensorProto` has external data support, but <https://github.com/onnx/onnx/blob/a952ab0e15884f4aa1d67ef935c3e691ae78c061/onnx/common/tensor.h#L24> does not. The version converter works on a `Graph` and not a `GraphProto`, so the conversions back and forth to protobuf destroy the external data references.
